title: AlphaFold2 from protein-structure prediction bottleneck to database-scale predicted structures
sourceNativeSummary: AlphaFold2 is both an algorithmic and infrastructure trajectory: blind evaluation established a step change, but database-scale public realization and confidence-aware use converted that result into a new scientific observation/representation substrate.
rivalOrBoundary: The trajectory separates model breakthrough, evaluation, database-scale materialization, scientific adoption and limits of prediction versus experimental reality.

pressure: Experimental determination of protein structures is slow and expensive relative to the enormous and growing sequence universe; decades of computational work had not made sequence-to-structure prediction reliably competitive across hard targets.
preExistingWorldModel: CASP provided a recurring blind benchmark against experimentally determined structures. Deep-learning methods and evolutionary sequence information were already improving predictions, while AlphaFold1 had shown progress before the 2020 CASP14 step change.
candidateRoutes: continue physics/energy-based simulation as the main general route
combine evolutionary/MSA information with deep learned geometric representations
scale end-to-end learned structure prediction and benchmark it blind on CASP
treat computational models only as narrow adjuncts to crystallography/cryo-EM rather than a large-scale structural resource
observationsAndInstruments: At CASP14 in 2020 AlphaFold2 achieved a step change in blind structure prediction sufficient for the 2024 Nobel committee to describe the long-standing prediction problem as solved in the relevant sense.
The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, launched with EMBL-EBI in 2021, expanded from model performance into a public infrastructure containing predictions for more than 200 million proteins.

By 2026 the database/model ecosystem continued to add complex predictions and serve a large research community, showing that the scientific result became a reusable data service rather than remaining a benchmark event.
decisiveTests: blind CASP accuracy against structures unavailable to the model builders
utility of predictions across proteins not optimized as a small hand-picked set
downstream scientific use while preserving confidence/experimental-validation boundaries
technicalOrScientificTransition: A high-performing prediction model crossed into scientific infrastructure when predictions could be generated at proteome scale, confidence-qualified, distributed openly and consumed by researchers without rerunning the original model-development process.
complements: large sequence databases and multiple-sequence alignments
rivalsAndFailures: Prediction does not replace all experimental structural biology: dynamics, ligands, complexes, disorder and uncertain regions can require other evidence.
A benchmark breakthrough alone would not create a durable research substrate without scale, access and confidence representation.
diffusionAndScaling: The trajectory moved from a competition result to hundreds of millions of predicted structures exposed as a shared scientific resource.
standardsAndInstitutions: DeepMind owned model development; CASP supplied independent blind evaluation; EMBL-EBI co-operated the public database; experimental repositories remained separate evidence authorities.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Prediction confidence, database coverage and experimentally verified structure remain distinct standings; broad availability can also propagate model/systematic errors at scale if confidence is ignored.
secondOrderEffects: Structure prediction altered the cost of asking structure-informed biological questions, shifting bottlenecks toward function, interaction, dynamics, experiment selection and interpretation.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement was rate-limiting at each lifecycle phase?
Which later success narrative compresses failures, rivals or distributed contributions?
